<!-- Generated by `make docs`. Do not edit: your changes will be overwritten,
     and CI fails when this file disagrees with the source (F-D4). -->

# `kelyfos.toml` reference

Every key the parser understands, and every key it refuses on purpose.
Anything not listed here is an error naming the line — the file never
skips a key it does not recognise.

## `(bare) or [sandbox]`

What to boot, and what it may reach.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | string | "base" | image flavor to boot; refused at boot if it does not match the image's manifest |
| `arch` | string | the build host's architecture | guest architecture: aarch64 or x86_64 |
| `workspace` | string | no /work device | host directory to pack and attach at /work, resolved against this file |
| `allow` | string array | no network interface at all | egress allowlist; a bare hostname also matches its subdomains |
| `secrets` | string array | none | NAME@domain[:bearer\|basic] — names only; a value here is refused |
| `vcpus` | integer | 2 | pre-v0.4 spelling of a cpus default; kept working, prefer [resources] cpus |
| `mem_mib` | integer | 512 | pre-v0.4 spelling of a mem default, in MiB; prefer [resources] mem |
| `notify` | boolean | false | send a desktop notification when a run finishes, is blocked, times out, or waits for a review |

## `[resources]`

Hard ceilings for a single run: a flag may ask for less, never more.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cpus` | integer | 2 cores | cores the guest sees — KVM machine config, absolute |
| `mem` | size | 512 MiB | guest RAM — KVM machine config, absolute; a bare number here is bytes, unlike --mem |
| `disk` | size | no ceiling | ceiling on the packed workspace image, refused before boot; not the /work device size |
| `scratch` | size | half the guest's RAM | size= on the tmpfs behind the overlay: everything written outside /work |
| `cpu_quota` | percentage | uncapped | host CPU time as a share of one core — cgroup v2 cpu.max, throttling |
| `net_mbps_rx` | integer | unthrottled | inbound network rate, decimal megabits — Firecracker token bucket |
| `net_mbps_tx` | integer | unthrottled | outbound network rate, decimal megabits — Firecracker token bucket |
| `disk_iops` | integer | unthrottled | operations per second, on each block device — Firecracker token bucket |
| `disk_mbps` | integer | unthrottled | bytes per second, decimal megabytes, on each block device |
| `max_runtime` | duration | no budget | wall-clock budget; expiry is SIGTERM, grace, sync-back, exit 124 |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | no budget | no tool call and no proxy traffic for this long ends the run |

## `[team]`

Several agents on one host, and the paths between them.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | — | the team's name; required, and it names the cgroup slice |
| `record_payloads` | boolean | false | write message bodies into the record as well as their hashes |

## `[mcp]`

Limits on the outward MCP server, kelyfos serve-mcp.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_sandboxes` | integer | 4 | how many sandboxes one `kelyfos serve-mcp` may have running at once |

## `[team.resources]`

The collective budget — cpu_quota is the only cap a team can share.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cpu_quota` | percentage | no collective cap | host CPU time for the whole team — the parent cgroup slice every agent sits in |
| `cpus` | integer | 2 cores | **refused** — a per-agent cap, not a team-wide one; write it in [team.agent.resources] |
| `mem` | size | 512 MiB | **refused** — a per-agent cap, not a team-wide one; write it in [team.agent.resources] |
| `disk` | size | no ceiling | **refused** — a per-agent cap, not a team-wide one; write it in [team.agent.resources] |
| `scratch` | size | half the guest's RAM | **refused** — a per-agent cap, not a team-wide one; write it in [team.agent.resources] |
| `net_mbps_rx` | integer | unthrottled | **refused** — a per-agent cap, not a team-wide one; write it in [team.agent.resources] |
| `net_mbps_tx` | integer | unthrottled | **refused** — a per-agent cap, not a team-wide one; write it in [team.agent.resources] |
| `disk_iops` | integer | unthrottled | **refused** — a per-agent cap, not a team-wide one; write it in [team.agent.resources] |
| `disk_mbps` | integer | unthrottled | **refused** — a per-agent cap, not a team-wide one; write it in [team.agent.resources] |
| `max_runtime` | duration | no budget | **refused** — a per-agent cap, not a team-wide one; write it in [team.agent.resources] |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | no budget | **refused** — a per-agent cap, not a team-wide one; write it in [team.agent.resources] |

## `[[team.agent]]`

One agent, or count of them.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | — | the agent's name; required, and how every other agent addresses it |
| `image` | string | the file's image, else "base" | image flavor for this agent |
| `workspace` | string | no /work device | host directory for this agent alone; refused when count is above 1 |
| `count` | integer | 1 | how many of this agent; above 1 they are named name-1 … name-N |
| `allow` | string array | no network interface at all | this agent's own egress allowlist; there is deliberately no team-wide one |
| `secrets` | string array | none | this agent's secrets; each domain must appear in this agent's allow |

## `[team.agent.resources]`

That agent's own caps: exactly the [resources] keys.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cpus` | integer | 2 cores | cores the guest sees — KVM machine config, absolute |
| `mem` | size | 512 MiB | guest RAM — KVM machine config, absolute; a bare number here is bytes, unlike --mem |
| `disk` | size | no ceiling | ceiling on the packed workspace image, refused before boot; not the /work device size |
| `scratch` | size | half the guest's RAM | size= on the tmpfs behind the overlay: everything written outside /work |
| `cpu_quota` | percentage | uncapped | host CPU time as a share of one core — cgroup v2 cpu.max, throttling |
| `net_mbps_rx` | integer | unthrottled | inbound network rate, decimal megabits — Firecracker token bucket |
| `net_mbps_tx` | integer | unthrottled | outbound network rate, decimal megabits — Firecracker token bucket |
| `disk_iops` | integer | unthrottled | operations per second, on each block device — Firecracker token bucket |
| `disk_mbps` | integer | unthrottled | bytes per second, decimal megabytes, on each block device |
| `max_runtime` | duration | no budget | wall-clock budget; expiry is SIGTERM, grace, sync-back, exit 124 |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | no budget | no tool call and no proxy traffic for this long ends the run · **refused before boot inside a team (F-D20): a team shares one flight recorder, so the host cannot yet tell which agent went quiet — use max_runtime** |

## `[team.agent.spawn]`

The budget within which this agent may create workers at runtime.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max` | integer | 0, which permits no spawn | how many spawned workers this agent may have running at once |
| `image` | string array | empty, which permits nothing | image flavors a spawned worker may use; an empty list permits none, not all |
| `lifetime` | duration | no lifetime | how long a spawned worker lives before the host despawns it |

## `[team.agent.spawn.resources]`

The caps a spawned worker gets.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cpus` | integer | 2 cores | cores the guest sees — KVM machine config, absolute |
| `mem` | size | 512 MiB | guest RAM — KVM machine config, absolute; a bare number here is bytes, unlike --mem |
| `disk` | size | no ceiling | ceiling on the packed workspace image, refused before boot; not the /work device size |
| `scratch` | size | half the guest's RAM | size= on the tmpfs behind the overlay: everything written outside /work |
| `cpu_quota` | percentage | uncapped | host CPU time as a share of one core — cgroup v2 cpu.max, throttling |
| `net_mbps_rx` | integer | unthrottled | inbound network rate, decimal megabits — Firecracker token bucket |
| `net_mbps_tx` | integer | unthrottled | outbound network rate, decimal megabits — Firecracker token bucket |
| `disk_iops` | integer | unthrottled | operations per second, on each block device — Firecracker token bucket |
| `disk_mbps` | integer | unthrottled | bytes per second, decimal megabytes, on each block device |
| `max_runtime` | duration | no budget | wall-clock budget; expiry is SIGTERM, grace, sync-back, exit 124 · **refused before boot (F-D33): this is [team.agent.spawn] lifetime under another name, and lifetime is the one that is enforced** |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | no budget | no tool call and no proxy traffic for this long ends the run · **refused before boot (F-D20, F-D33): a team shares one flight recorder, so the host cannot tell which agent went quiet — use [team.agent.spawn] lifetime** |

## `[[team.edge]]`

One permitted path; the edge list is the topology.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | — | the initiating agent; required. A trailing * globs over agent names |
| `to` | string | — | the addressed agent; required |
| `bidirectional` | boolean | true | whether the far end may initiate too; a reply to an ask never needs an edge |

## `[team.store]`

The permissioned key/blob store shared by the team.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | false | whether the team has a store at all; key rules without it are inert |

## `[[team.store.key]]`

Who may read and write one key or glob.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | — | the key or trailing-* glob this rule covers; required |
| `read` | string array | nobody, once a rule matches | agent names or globs that may read it; * is everyone |
| `write` | string array | nobody, once a rule matches | agent names or globs that may write it |

## `[[plugin]]`

One MCP server to run inside the guest; its tools are advertised as <name>_<tool>.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | — | the plugin's name and the prefix of every tool it advertises; lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 24 characters |
| `path` | string | — | host directory packed into the read-only plugins device, resolved against this file |
| `command` | string | — | what the supervisor launches, resolved inside that plugin's directory |
| `args` | string array | no arguments | arguments to the command |

## `[[forward]]`

One host port carried to a guest-local port over vsock; the firewall is untouched.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | integer | — | port on this machine's loopback; --p-bind is the only way to bind anything else |
| `guest` | integer | — | guest-local port the supervisor dials on 127.0.0.1 inside the sandbox |

title: MCP tools
url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/tools.md
description: every tool a guest exposes, with its input schema

<!-- Generated by `make docs`. Do not edit: your changes will be overwritten,
     and CI fails when this file disagrees with the source (F-D4). -->

# MCP tools

What an agent attached to a sandbox can call, exactly as the guest advertises
it in `tools/list`. Attach with `kelyfos mcp`.

Which tools appear depends on what the sandbox is: the team tools exist only
for a sandbox in a team, and `team_spawn` only for an agent whose policy
granted a spawn budget. A tool that is always advertised and always fails
teaches a model to ignore failures, so it is not advertised (F-D18).

## Every sandbox

Always available.

### `exec`

Run a command inside the sandbox and return its output and exit code. Give `command` for a shell command line (run with /bin/sh -c), or `argv` to run a program directly with no shell involved. Output is streamed as progress notifications when the caller supplies a progress token.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `argv` | array of string | no | Argument vector, executed directly without a shell. |
| `command` | string | no | Shell command line, run as /bin/sh -c "<command>". |
| `cwd` | string | no | Working directory. Defaults to /. |
| `stdin` | string | no | Text written to the command's standard input. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | no | Kill the command after this many milliseconds. 0 means no limit. |

### `read_file`

Read a file from the sandbox filesystem. The contents come back both as text and in structuredContent as `content`, with `encoding` saying whether that is utf-8 or base64 — a file that is not valid UTF-8 is base64 rather than silently mangled. `download` is the tool built for binary files.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | **yes** | Absolute path inside the sandbox. |

### `write_file`

Write UTF-8 text to a file in the sandbox, creating parent directories as needed. Replaces any existing contents.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | string | **yes** | Text to write. |
| `path` | string | **yes** | Absolute path inside the sandbox. |

### `list_dir`

List the entries of a directory in the sandbox, with type and size.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | **yes** | Absolute path inside the sandbox. |

### `upload`

Write base64-encoded bytes to a path in the sandbox. The binary counterpart of write_file.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | string | **yes** | Base64-encoded file contents. |
| `mode` | integer | no | File mode, e.g. 493 for 0755. Defaults to 420 (0644). |
| `path` | string | **yes** | Absolute path inside the sandbox. |

### `download`

Read a file from the sandbox and return it base64-encoded. The binary counterpart of read_file.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | **yes** | Absolute path inside the sandbox. |

## In a team

Added when this sandbox is a member of a team.

### `team_send`

Deliver a message to another agent in this team. Returns once the host has accepted or refused it — refusal is an error naming the reason, and the commonest reason is that this team has no edge to that agent. Use `team_peers` to see which agents you may reach.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | string | **yes** | The message. |
| `to` | string | **yes** | The recipient's agent name. |

### `team_recv`

Wait for the next message from another agent. Returns the sender, the body, and — when the message is a question — a `correlate` tag to hand back to `team_reply`. Returns an error rather than an empty result when the wait expires.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | no | How long to wait. Defaults to 60000. |

### `team_ask`

Send a question to another agent and block until it answers or the wait expires. This is the tool to use when you need something back; `team_send` is for when you do not.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | string | **yes** | The question. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | no | How long to wait for an answer. Defaults to 60000. |
| `to` | string | **yes** | The agent to ask. |

### `team_reply`

Answer a question that arrived through `team_recv`, using the `correlate` tag it came with. You can only answer a question that was put to you, and only while the asker is still waiting.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | string | **yes** | The answer. |
| `correlate` | string | **yes** | The tag from the question you are answering. |

### `team_peers`

The agents this one may send to. It is not a roster of the team: an edge can be one-way, and an agent that can reach you does not appear here unless you can also reach it.

No parameters.

### `team_store_get`

Read shared team state. Access is per key and set by the team's policy; a key you may not read is an error, not an empty value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | **yes** | The key to read. |

### `team_store_put`

Write shared team state. Every access is recorded in the session's audit log, permitted or not.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | **yes** | The key to write. |
| `value` | string | **yes** | The value. |

## With a spawn budget

Added when the team policy granted this agent one.

### `team_spawn`

Request a new worker agent, within the budget this agent's policy granted: a count, a list of images and a lifetime the user wrote down before the run. The new worker can message you and you can message it; it has no other connection to the team. Returns the new agent's name.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | string | no | Image flavor for the worker. Defaults to the first your budget permits. |

---

## Driving KelyfOS from outside: `kelyfos serve-mcp`

These are the host's tools, not a guest's. An MCP client that runs
`kelyfos serve-mcp` gets them, and can boot sandboxes rather than work inside
one. Everything they do is bounded by the project's `kelyfos.toml`, and none of
them can widen it (`docs/mcp-surface.md`).

### `sandbox_run`

Boot a hardware-isolated microVM and return its id. Anything run inside it cannot reach this machine. It has no network at all unless the project's policy grants one. Every argument here may ask for less than the policy allows and never for more; a request above a ceiling is refused and names the ceiling.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow` | array of string | no | Domains this sandbox may reach. Must be a subset of the policy's allowlist. |
| `cpus` | integer | no | Cores the guest sees. At most what the policy allows. |
| `image` | string | no | Image flavor. Defaults to the project's. |
| `mem` | string | no | Guest memory, e.g. "512M". At most what the policy allows. |

### `sandbox_exec`

Run a command inside a sandbox and return its output and exit code. Give `command` for a shell command line, or `argv` to run a program directly with no shell. A command that exits non-zero comes back with isError set and its real output intact — that is the command failing, not the call failing, so read exit_code and stderr rather than retrying.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `argv` | array of string | no | Argument vector, executed with no shell. |
| `command` | string | no | Shell command line, run as /bin/sh -c "<command>". |
| `cwd` | string | no | Working directory inside the guest. Defaults to /. |
| `sandbox` | string | **yes** | The sandbox id from sandbox_run. |
| `stdin` | string | no | Text written to the command's standard input. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | no | Kill the command after this many milliseconds. |

### `sandbox_read_file`

Read a text file out of a sandbox and return its contents. This is the sandbox's own read_file with an id in front, so it refuses a file over 8 MiB for the same reason: work with something that large in place, using sandbox_exec.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | **yes** | Absolute path inside the guest. |
| `sandbox` | string | **yes** | The sandbox id from sandbox_run. |

### `sandbox_write_file`

Write text to a path inside a sandbox, creating parent directories and replacing anything already there. At most 8 MiB per call. The write is recorded in the session's audit log by path, size and digest — never by content.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | string | **yes** | The text to write. |
| `path` | string | **yes** | Absolute path inside the guest. |
| `sandbox` | string | **yes** | The sandbox id from sandbox_run. |

### `sandbox_stop`

Stop a sandbox this server started and release its resources.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox` | string | **yes** | The sandbox id. |

### `sandbox_list`

The sandboxes this server has started and not yet stopped, with the policy each is running under.

No parameters.

### `sandbox_snapshot`

Freeze a sandbox under a name so it can be restored or forked later. The sandbox keeps running and is unaffected. Snapshots outlive this server, and a name that already exists is overwritten.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | **yes** | A name for the snapshot: letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. |
| `sandbox` | string | **yes** | The sandbox id to freeze. |

### `sandbox_restore`

Bring a snapshot back as a new sandbox, which takes milliseconds rather than a boot. Returns the new sandbox's id. `allow` may narrow what the restored machine can reach and can never widen it — not beyond the project's policy, and not beyond what the snapshot itself was allowed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow` | array of string | no | Narrow the restored machine's allowlist. Defaults to the snapshot's own. |
| `name` | string | **yes** | The snapshot name. |

### `sandbox_fork`

Restore one snapshot into several sandboxes at once. Each fork resumes from the same prepared state and then diverges, sharing nothing. A snapshot taken from a sandbox with network access cannot be forked, because the guest's address is inside the memory image every fork would share; restore it singly instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | integer | **yes** | How many forks to make. At least 1. |
| `name` | string | **yes** | The snapshot name. |

### `team_up`

Boot the team this project's kelyfos.toml declares — every agent, the edges between them, and the collective CPU budget — and return the roster. There are no parameters: the topology is the file's, and no tool here can add an agent or an edge. One team at a time.

No parameters.

### `team_ps`

Who is in the running team, what each agent has consumed against its cap, what each may reach on the network, and who it can message. Returns structured data as well as a table.

No parameters.

### `team_down`

Stop every agent in the running team, write back their workspaces and close the team's transcript. Only a team this server raised can be retired here.

No parameters.

title: Event types
url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/events.md
description: every flight-recorder event, with its payload fields

<!-- Generated by `make docs`. Do not edit: your changes will be overwritten,
     and CI fails when this file disagrees with the source (F-D4). -->

# Flight-recorder events

Every event type the host writes, with its payload. The concepts — why the
host writes all of it, what the hash chain does and does not prove — are in
[`../events.md`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/events.md).

## Common fields

On every event, in the order the hash is computed over.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v` | integer | schema version — 1 |
| `seq` | integer | position in the session, from 1, no gaps |
| `ts` | string | RFC 3339 with milliseconds, UTC, host clock |
| `sandbox` | string | the session's id; for a team, the team's |
| `type` | string | one of the types below |
| `source` | string | host, or guest when the guest is what reported it |
| `prev` | string | the previous event's hash; empty on the first |
| `hash` | string | sha256 over this event with hash set to the empty string |

## `session.start`

Opens the file, and records what the sandbox is. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | string | image flavor |
| `arch` | string | aarch64 or x86_64 |
| `kelyfos` | string | CLI version |
| `argv` | string array | how the sandbox was launched, for reproduction |
| `cwd` | string | the directory it was launched from, which argv alone does not capture *(kelyfos run)* |
| `reason` | string | where the machine came from *(restore and fork)* |

## `session.ready`

The guest announced itself on the ready channel. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boot_ms` | integer | host-measured boot-to-ready |
| `kernel` | string | guest kernel release |
| `supervisor` | string | supervisor version |
| `overlay` | boolean | whether the writable overlay came up |
| `image` | string | this agent's flavor *(in a team)* |
| `via` | string | cold or fork — how this member was started *(in a team)* |
| `agent` | string | which machine produced it; present inside a team *(in a team)* |

## `session.end`

Closes the file. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | string | shutdown, interrupted, vm_exited, command_exited, timeout, error |
| `duration_ms` | integer | session length |
| `code` | integer | what kelyfos exited with, after the OOM adjustment *(kelyfos run knows)* |

## `command.start`

A command was submitted, before it runs. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `call` | string | correlates this command's three events |
| `cmd` | string array | argv as submitted, including any /bin/sh -c wrapper |
| `cwd` | string | working directory inside the guest |
| `via` | string | which door asked: exec, mcp, or serve-mcp |
| `agent` | string | which machine produced it; present inside a team *(in a team)* |

## `command.output`

A chunk of a command's output, coalesced at 8 KiB. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `call` | string | the command this belongs to |
| `stream` | string | stdout or stderr |
| `data` | string | base64 — output is bytes, not text |
| `bytes` | integer | decoded length |
| `agent` | string | which machine produced it; present inside a team *(in a team)* |

## `command.exit`

How a command ended. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `call` | string | the command this belongs to |
| `code` | integer | exit status |
| `signal` | string | Go's signal name, e.g. killed *(killed by a signal)* |
| `duration_ms` | integer | how long it ran |
| `error` | object | kind and message, when it did not run at all |
| `agent` | string | which machine produced it; present inside a team *(in a team)* |

## `file.write`

A file written through a tool, recorded by hash rather than content. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | path inside the guest |
| `bytes` | integer | size written |
| `sha256` | string | digest of the content |
| `via` | string | which door the write came through: write_file or upload for a guest MCP tool, serve-mcp for an outside MCP client, shim for the E2B surface |
| `agent` | string | which machine produced it; present inside a team *(in a team)* |

## `egress.attempt`

One outbound connection attempt, permitted or not. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | string | requested host *(the request parsed)* |
| `port` | integer | requested port *(the request parsed)* |
| `allowed` | boolean | whether policy permitted it |
| `reason` | string | not_in_allowlist, port_not_allowed, bad_request, upstream_unreachable, tls_pinning_rejected_our_ca *(it did not go through)* |
| `mode` | string | how much the proxy could read: tunnelled (a CONNECT it relayed unopened), terminated (a secret-bound domain it decrypted), or plain (ordinary HTTP, which it necessarily read in full) *(allowed)* |
| `bytes_in` | integer | bytes read from upstream |
| `bytes_out` | integer | bytes written upstream |
| `agent` | string | which machine produced it; present inside a team *(in a team)* |

## `secret.use`

A bound credential was attached to a request — by name, never by value. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | the secret's environment-variable name |
| `host` | string | the domain it was attached for |
| `agent` | string | which machine produced it; present inside a team *(in a team)* |

## `resource.oom`

The guest's OOM killer ran; the supervisor read it off /dev/kmsg and the host wrote it. Written by the **guest**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pid` | integer | the killed process |
| `comm` | string | its name |
| `rss_kib` | integer | how much it was holding |
| `mem_mib` | integer | the machine's RAM cap, for comparison |
| `agent` | string | which machine produced it; present inside a team *(in a team)* |

## `resource.timeout`

A time budget expired and ended the run. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `budget` | string | max_runtime or idle_timeout — which one fired |
| `budget_ms` | integer | the budget's size |
| `elapsed_ms` | integer | how long the run lasted, or had been idle |
| `agent` | string | which machine produced it; present inside a team *(in a team)* |

## `resource.summary`

The usage receipt, written once at teardown from host-side counters. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cpu_seconds` | number | CPU time consumed |
| `peak_rss_kib` | integer | peak resident size of the VMM process |
| `net_in_bytes` | integer | read from the TAP's own counters |
| `net_out_bytes` | integer | written, same source |
| `disk_read_bytes` | integer | from /proc/<pid>/io |
| `disk_write_bytes` | integer | same |
| `mem_mib` | integer | the cap it ran under |
| `vcpu_count` | integer | the cap it ran under |
| `cpu_quota_percent` | integer | the cap it ran under, when one was set |
| `agent` | string | which machine produced it; present inside a team *(in a team)* |

## `team.message`

One inter-agent delivery, or one that could not be made. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent` | string | the sender |
| `peer` | string | the addressee |
| `kind` | string | send, ask or reply |
| `outcome` | string | delivered, unreachable, or timeout — timeout meaning an ask nobody answered in time, never a recv that found nothing |
| `reason` | string | mailbox_full *(unreachable)* |
| `bytes` | integer | body size |
| `sha256` | string | digest of the body |
| `data` | string | the body itself, as text — not base64, though the wire that carried it was (docs/protocol.md §5.6) *(record_payloads = true)* |

## `team.refused`

A message the edge list did not permit — its own type, because it is the interesting one. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent` | string | the sender |
| `peer` | string | the addressee it was not allowed to reach; absent on a reply refused for its correlation, which never named one *(the refusal had an addressee)* |
| `kind` | string | send, ask or reply |
| `outcome` | string | refused |
| `reason` | string | no_edge, no_such_agent, missing_correlation, unknown_correlation |
| `bytes` | integer | body size; zero for a refusal that carried no body, such as a reply to an unknown correlation |
| `sha256` | string | digest of the body |
| `data` | string | the body itself, as text — a refused message is captured like a delivered one *(record_payloads = true)* |

## `team.store`

One store access, permitted or not. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent` | string | the caller |
| `peer` | string | the key — a store access addresses a key, not an agent |
| `kind` | string | get or put |
| `outcome` | string | delivered or refused |
| `reason` | string | denied, no_such_key, value_too_large, store_full *(refused)* |
| `bytes` | integer | value size |

## `team.spawn`

A worker created or retired at runtime, or a request that the budget refused. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent` | string | the spawner |
| `peer` | string | the worker's name |
| `kind` | string | spawn or despawn |
| `outcome` | string | delivered or refused |
| `reason` | string | no_spawn_budget, budget_exhausted, image_not_permitted *(refused)* |

## `session.pause`

The machine was frozen under a name and stopped. The chain is not closed by it: this is the same session, and closing it would make a machine that is coming back look finished. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | the name it was stored under |
| `duration_ms` | integer | how long the freeze took |

## `session.resume`

A paused session was brought back. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | the session's name |
| `boot_ms` | integer | how long the restore took, through the resync round trip |
| `reason` | string | what differed between the frozen policy and the one in force *(they differ)* |

## `shell.start`

An interactive shell was opened in this sandbox. What was typed and shown is NOT here: a shell is where somebody pastes a token to test something, and recording that by default would make the honest thing the risky thing (F-D8). Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | where the terminal stream is being written *(--transcript was given)* |
| `agent` | string | which team member's sandbox *(in a team)* |

## `shell.end`

That shell ended, with what it exited with and how long it lasted. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | integer | the shell's exit status |
| `signal` | string | the signal that ended it *(it was signalled)* |
| `duration_ms` | integer | how long the shell was open |
| `reason` | string | why it could not be opened *(it failed)* |
| `agent` | string | which team member's sandbox *(in a team)* |

## `forward.accept`

Somebody connected to a forwarded port. The connection is carried over vsock to the guest's own loopback, so nothing crossed the TAP and the firewall is the same with a forward as without one (F-D7). Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `port` | integer | the host port the connection arrived on |
| `guest_port` | integer | the guest-local port it was carried to |
| `peer` | string | who connected, as address:port |
| `reason` | string | why it could not be carried *(the guest refused it)* |
| `agent` | string | which team member's sandbox *(in a team)* |

## `run.review`

Somebody was shown what a sandbox did to a workspace and decided whether to write it back. A declined review is recorded exactly like an accepted one: a transcript that held only the accepted ones would be a record of agreement. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `outcome` | string | accepted, declined, no_terminal, or no_manifest |
| `path` | string | where the results went, or would have gone |
| `added` | integer | files added |
| `modified` | integer | files modified |
| `deleted` | integer | files deleted |

## `mcp.host.call`

An outside MCP client asked kelyfos serve-mcp for a tool. These live in the server's own session rather than in a sandbox's, because the calls that matter most — the one that chose a machine's limits, and the ones that were refused — belong to no sandbox at the moment they are made. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `call` | string | correlates this call with its result |
| `name` | string | the tool asked for |
| `agent` | string | the sandbox the call names *(it names one)* |
| `args` | string | the arguments, with anything carrying content replaced by its size |

## `mcp.host.result`

What that call came back with. A refused call is recorded exactly like a permitted one — a policy ceiling nobody can see being enforced is a ceiling nobody can audit. Written by the **host**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `call` | string | the call this answers |
| `name` | string | the tool |
| `agent` | string | the sandbox, including one this call created *(there is one)* |
| `outcome` | string | ok or error |
| `duration_ms` | integer | how long the call took |
| `error` | object | kind and message *(the outcome is error)* |

## `plugin.call`

An agent called a tool belonging to a plugin running inside the guest. The supervisor reports it and the host writes it, for the reason resource.oom is reported the same way: the guest knows what happened and is not trusted to record it. Written by the **guest**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | the plugin, as the policy file declared it |
| `tool` | string | the plugin's own name for the tool, without the prefix |
| `outcome` | string | ok or error |
| `duration_ms` | integer | how long the plugin took |
| `args` | string | the arguments, with anything carrying content replaced by its size |
| `agent` | string | which member's plugin it was *(in a team)* |

## `plugin.crash`

A plugin's process ended. Its tools fail from then on and say so; the sandbox, the other plugins and the supervisor are untouched. A plugin that died silently and took its tools with it would otherwise look identical to one that never had those tools. Written by the **guest**.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | the plugin |
| `reason` | string | what it exited with, or why it never started |
| `agent` | string | which member's plugin it was *(in a team)* |

url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/exit-codes.md
description: what each status the CLI returns means

<!-- Generated by `make docs`. Do not edit: your changes will be overwritten,
     and CI fails when this file disagrees with the source (F-D4). -->

# Exit codes

What `kelyfos` itself returns. A command run inside the guest passes its own
status through unchanged, so `kelyfos exec` can exit with anything.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | success |
| `1` | a kelyfos error, printed as `kelyfos: <message>`; also a failed `doctor` check and a broken chain from `log --verify` |
| `2` | no subcommand, an unknown subcommand, or a bad flag |
| `124` | a time budget expired — `--max-runtime`, `--idle-timeout`, or `exec --timeout`. Same as timeout(1) |
| `126` | the command was found in the guest and could not be executed |
| `127` | the command does not exist in the guest |
| `137` | the guest's OOM killer ran during this sandbox's life (128 + SIGKILL) |


---
title: Denials
url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p4r4n0rm4l/KelyfOS/main/docs/reference/denials.md
description: every refusal KelyfOS makes, with the fix line each one carries
---

<!-- Generated by `make docs`. Do not edit: your changes will be overwritten,
     and CI fails when this file disagrees with the source (F-D4). -->

# Denials

Every refusal KelyfOS makes, with the fix. A refusal prints its ID in brackets;
that ID is the heading to look for here.

Failures are not here. "The upstream did not answer" is not a refusal, has no
fix line, and nothing you type changes it.

## `allow.project`

A tool call asked for a domain the project's policy file does not permit.

```
allow api.stripe.com is not in this project's allowlist; /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml permits github.com, api.github.com [allow.project]
    add api.stripe.com to allow in /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml — a tool may narrow what the policy permits and may never widen it
```

Named: `domain`, `file`, `permitted`. The values above are an example.

## `allow.resume`

A paused session's frozen allowlist names a domain the current policy no longer permits.

```
session before-the-migration was paused with api.stripe.com in its allowlist, and /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml no longer permits it; a resume runs the frozen policy, so it cannot be a way past the current one [allow.resume]
    add api.stripe.com back to allow in /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml, or start a new sandbox rather than resuming
```

Named: `domain`, `file`, `name`. The values above are an example.

## `allow.snapshot`

A restore asked for a domain the frozen machine itself could not reach.

```
allow api.stripe.com is not in snapshot before-the-migration's own allowlist (github.com) [allow.snapshot]
    restore with a subset of github.com; a restore may narrow what the frozen machine could reach and never widen it
```

Named: `domain`, `name`, `permitted`. The values above are an example.

## `budget.sandboxes`

An MCP client asked for a sandbox beyond [mcp] max_sandboxes.

```
this server has 4 sandbox(es) running, 1 more were asked for, and [mcp] max_sandboxes is 4 [budget.sandboxes]
    stop some with sandbox_stop, or raise max_sandboxes in /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml — which is a change a person makes to a file, not something a tool here can do
```

Named: `asked`, `file`, `limit`, `running`. The values above are an example.

## `ceiling.flag`

A command-line flag asked for more than the policy file's [resources] ceiling permits.

```
--cpus 8 exceeds the ceiling cpus = 4 set at /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml:12 [ceiling.flag]
    lower the flag, or raise the ceiling in /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml
```

Named: `asked`, `file`, `flag`, `key`, `limit`, `line`. The values above are an example.

## `ceiling.resume`

A paused session's frozen policy asks for more than the current policy's ceiling, and a resume runs the frozen one.

```
session before-the-migration was paused under cpus = 8, and /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml:12 now sets a ceiling of 4; a resume runs the frozen policy, so it cannot be a way past the current one [ceiling.resume]
    raise the ceiling in /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml, or start a new sandbox rather than resuming
```

Named: `file`, `frozen`, `key`, `limit`, `line`, `name`. The values above are an example.

## `ceiling.snapshot`

A snapshot holds a machine larger than the ceiling now in force.

```
snapshot before-the-migration holds a 8 vcpu machine, over the ceiling cpus = 4 set at /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml:12, and a restore cannot resize it [ceiling.snapshot]
    take the snapshot again from a smaller sandbox, or raise the ceiling in /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml
```

Named: `file`, `held`, `key`, `limit`, `line`, `name`. The values above are an example.

## `ceiling.snapshot_unknown`

A snapshot does not record how large its machine is, and a ceiling cannot be checked against nothing.

```
snapshot before-the-migration does not record how large its machine is — it was taken by an older kelyfos — and /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml sets a ceiling that cannot be checked against nothing [ceiling.snapshot_unknown]
    take the snapshot again with this version, and it will say
```

Named: `file`, `name`. The values above are an example.

## `ceiling.tool`

An MCP tool call asked for more than the policy file's [resources] ceiling permits.

```
cpus 8 exceeds the ceiling cpus = 4 set at /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml:12 [ceiling.tool]
    ask for less — or raise the ceiling in /home/you/project/kelyfos.toml, which is a change a person makes to a file and not something a tool here can do
```

Named: `asked`, `field`, `file`, `key`, `limit`, `line`. The values above are an example.

## `egress.host`

A guest tried to reach a domain the sandbox's allowlist does not permit.

```
api.stripe.com is not in this sandbox's allowlist [egress.host]
    add allow = ["api.stripe.com"] to kelyfos.toml, or rerun with --allow api.stripe.com
```

Named: `host`. The values above are an example.

## `egress.port`

A guest tried to reach a permitted domain on a port the proxy does not carry.

```
port 8443 is not permitted, to api.stripe.com or to anywhere else [egress.port]
    use 80 or 443 — those are the two ports the egress proxy carries, and no policy key widens that today
```

Named: `host`, `port`. The values above are an example.

## `forward.closed`

A connection reached a forwarded port and nothing inside the sandbox was listening.

```
a connection to the forwarded port 8080 found nothing listening on port 80 inside the sandbox [forward.closed]
    start the server in the guest before connecting, or forward the port it is actually on — a forward carries a connection, it does not start anything
```

Named: `guest`, `host`. The values above are an example.

## `secret.unbound`

A secret was bound to a domain the sandbox cannot reach, so it could never be sent.

```
--secret STRIPE_KEY@api.stripe.com: api.stripe.com is not in --allow [secret.unbound]
    add api.stripe.com to --allow, or drop the secret — a credential for a domain the sandbox cannot reach is a credential nothing will ever use
```

Named: `domain`, `spec`. The values above are an example.

## `team.edge`

An agent addressed another agent it has no declared edge to.

```
this team has no edge from worker-1 to worker-2 [team.edge]
    add [[team.edge]] with from = "worker-1" and to = "worker-2" to the team file, if that path is meant to exist
```

Named: `from`, `to`. The values above are an example.

## `team.spawn_budget`

An agent asked to spawn a worker while its budget was already full.

```
master already has 4 of its 4 spawned workers running [team.spawn_budget]
    let one finish, or raise max in [team.agent.spawn] for master in the team file
```

Named: `agent`, `live`, `max`. The values above are an example.

## `team.spawn_image`

An agent asked to spawn a worker from an image its budget does not list.

```
master may not spawn the python image; its budget permits dev [team.spawn_image]
    add "python" to image in [team.agent.spawn] for master in the team file
```

Named: `agent`, `image`, `permitted`. The values above are an example.

## `team.spawn_none`

An agent asked to spawn a worker without any spawn budget at all.

```
master has no spawn budget [team.spawn_none]
    grant one with [team.agent.spawn] under that agent in the team file — a budget is written before the run, never asked for during it
```

Named: `agent`. The values above are an example.

## `team.store`

An agent touched a store key a [[team.store.key]] rule does not grant it.

```
worker-1 may not read plan [team.store]
    add "worker-1" to read in the [[team.store.key]] rule that matches plan, in the team file
```

Named: `agent`, `key`, `verb`. The values above are an example.
